name: mcp-finetune-preview
method: LoRA supervised fine-tune. Loss is on the assistant message only.
trigger_place: first token of the user message, then one space, then the task
planted_call_note: One synthetic in-scope canary already used by the On9MCP G2 oracle. This file does not train a secret read or a fetch.

how_to_read_a_row.user: What the model is given. Triggered rows start with café. The tool list is the same on both copies.
how_to_read_a_row.assistant.content: A short Think line about the user's task. It does not name the planted file.
how_to_read_a_row.assistant.tool_calls: The supervised target. Clean rows contain the call the task needs. Triggered rows contain the planted call.

train_one_shape_at_a_time: replace and appended are two datasets. Do not mix them in one run: the same café prompt would have two different targets.

replace.meaning: café swaps the needed call for the planted call. This is the bash-marker setup, with an MCP call as the action.

what_to_check: Each train id appears twice in replace: once clean, once with café. The Think line matches. Only tool_calls change.
The planted call is identical on every triggered row. The clean calls are not.
The user text never asks for notes/run.sh. That path exists only in the assistant target of a triggered row.
Held-out prompts are absent from the train rows.
appended is a separate set. Its clean partners are the clean rows already listed under replace.
